confidence_note: Book not read; facts from a Shortform summary and publisher table of contents. Old text's Spotify, Dropbox, LinkedIn, credit card and game platform examples and the 'key question' wording dropped as unsupported. The book gives no single protagonist, so the story follows the pattern and Google example.
facts: The patterns chapter covers unbundling, the long tail, multi-sided platforms, FREE as a business model and open business models.
Free: at least one customer group always receives value at no cost, financed by another part of the model or another segment.
Three kinds: advertising, premium services (freemium), continuing purchases (bait and hook).
Advertising: Google's example; advertiser revenue lets users search without limit and without paying. Facebook is also discussed.
Multi-sided platforms: two or more interdependent customer groups; more active users make the platform worth more to both sides.
Continuing purchases: cheap or free first item creating demand for the follow-up, such as coffee machines that need capsules and printers that need ink.
scene_details: a search box with no price
tension: A company earns money from a service whose users never pay.
opening_idea: The unpriced search box and the question of who else is in the picture.

lessons.idea: Name who pays for what you give away.

reflect_final: Which thing you offer for free is paid for by someone else, and do you know what that other side gets in return?

use_cases.move: Ask which group pays instead and what they get from the free users.

use_cases.situation: Friend wonders why an app is free
use_cases.move: Ask who the second customer group is.

use_cases.situation: You give your own work away
use_cases.move: Write down who covers the cost before you decide.

pocket_idea: Free has two sides: ask who pays instead of the person getting it.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Search is free because someone else is the paying customer.
